application_review: PROGRESS. Prior audit rechecked and all retained proof hashes unchanged.
The product perturbation bound is proved by finite-set induction for two unit-bounded real factor families. It sums actual factor differences and does not divide by potentially zero factors.
The pointwise dual bound keeps the original short cube-direction Haar average and exact nonroot vertex sum.

Interchanging root and direction averages and translating the root identifies every vertex error with the original input L1 error. The exact number of nonroot vertices gives the factor 2^d-1, including dimension zero.
The squared-error bound uses the proved unit bounds on both actual dual functions, giving output L2 squared at most 2*(2^d-1) times input L1. Constants are uniform in all finite groups and subgroups.
Six new theorems are individually audited. These justify perturbation in prospective approximation arguments; no higher-order concatenation or Bessel conclusion is assumed or claimed.
